text: We evaluated an evolution-strategy refinement method that uses swap-consistency as its fitness signal, with an ES population of 8, transferring supervision from a gpt2-large weak model to a qwen2.5-3b strong model. Across num_seeds = 2, the weak supervisor reached 0.54 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.71, while the transfer accuracy came to 0.58 with a standard error of 0.03. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.25 with a standard error of 0.17, against a baseline PGR of 0.16. Because the measured PGR sits well within two standard errors of the baseline, this run does not support a claim that the method improves on the baseline; the apparent ordering could easily reflect seed noise. The two-seed sample is also too small to characterize variance dependably, so the PGR standard error of 0.17 should itself be treated as a rough indication. Further seeds are needed before any directional conclusion is drawn.
